newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota crops receive needed warmth, rain.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota crops receive needed warmth, rain.

text.p: Crops in Minnesota were boosted by warmer weather during the last few days of May and about half the state received much-needed rain, according to the Minnesota Agricultural Statistics Service.
"May was unusually dry and cold in Minnesota, but the month ended with several days of above-normal temperatures which warmed soils rapidly," the report said.
The condition of spring wheat improved sharply to 76 percent good to excellent, up from 49 percent a week earlier. Spring wheat was 91 percent planted as of Sunday, up from 66 percent a week ago.

Corn was 99 percent planted and 80 percent emerged, up from 97 and 46 percent respectively a week ago. Corn was rated five percent excellent, 47 percent good, 38 percent fair, nine percent poor and one percent very poor.
Soybeans were 91 percent planted and 31 percent emerged, up from 82 percent and eight percent a week earlier.
Topsoil moisture, as of Friday, was rated eight percent surplus, 64 percent adequate, 19 percent short and nine percent very short.
